thread:
anne: Quick sync — sketching a preemptive-eviction + surge-fairness approach for the policy engine. want feedback on semantics and runtime boundary.

anne: problem: during cross-tenant spikes some low-latency tenants get starved by noisy heavy ones; current soft-degrade simply drops to cheaper model which still costs latency. we need deterministic, fair admission that keeps p95 for high-tier tenants while limiting cost.

sahil: high-level: prefer a credit-based admission where each tenant has an "allocation credit" replenished by SLA tier and historical usage. during spikes, eviction picks requests that would not violate p95 for higher-credit tenants.

maria: tie-breaks are tricky. do credits reset per-region? what about multi-region HA where a tenant bursts in one region but is idle in another?

kevin: propose: credits are per-tenant-per-region with a small global bucket for cross-region handoff. that way we can preempt locally without global churn. also add a soft-degrade window (configurable) so you can let short spikes through.

lia: runtime boundary: is this policy engine concern or router concern? we need low-latency decisions (<1ms) for admission. can't call heavy sim or DB lookups on every request.

anne: design thought: policy service exposes a compact decision API (stateless): input = {tenant_id, region, estimated_cost, latency_budgets, token_count, priority_hint}. output = {admit:true|false, degrade_variant:optional, eviction_score:float}. router keeps local LRU cache of decisions + slot leases.

sahil: eviction_score needs to be stable and explainable. include factors: credit_ratio, recent_success_rate, upgrade_penalty, region_affinity. weight vector must be configurable and plumbed from operator console.

maria: can we compute eviction_score incrementally in the router using cached micro-signals to avoid RPCs? like keep counters for each tenant and recompute score with local weights. fallback to policy service for cold tenants.

kevin: yes — hybrid model. policy service publishes weight epochs and quotas, router applies them locally. only sync deltas. that keeps admission fast and centralizes complex logic.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed policy-service v0.9 to staging/region-eu at 2026-03-23T15:42Z :eyes:

lia: fallback semantics: if router's local decision differs from policy service due to staleness, what do we do? accept optimistic local decision or re-query? both have tradeoffs.

anne: proposal: optimistic-local OR recheck depending on request priority: for high-priority (gold) tenants recheck synchronously; for lower-priority rely on optimistic local decision and let metrics catch regressions. add audit log for every recheck to debug oscillations.

sahil: need simulation harness to stress-test fairness and cost. sim should model heterogeneous tenants (PLG small bursts, enterprise steady high qps). also model preemption latencies when evicting KV caches / KV cache warmups.

maria: add metrics we will track in sim: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, cost-per-req delta vs baseline, eviction-rate, warmup-penalty (tokens), and fairness index (e.g., Jain's index).

kevin: rollout plan: 1) implement local scoring + weight publish API; 2) add sim and run against production traces; 3) canary with low-impact tenants; 4) enable per-tenant overrides in Console.

lia: config snippet suggestion for weights (RFC form):

```
policy_weights:
  credit_ratio: 0.45
  recent_success_rate: 0.2
  upgrade_penalty: 0.15
  region_affinity: 0.1
  randomness_entropy: 0.1
```

anne: randomness_entropy is intentional to break ties and avoid pathological lockstep. small gaussian jitter at decision time.

sahil: security note: do not encode tenant secrets in scores. only reference tenant_id and public tier. audit logs must scrub PII.

maria: ops: how do we debug incidents where a tenant claims being throttled unfairly? need an explainability endpoint returning last N scores + contributing factors.

kevin: agree. include an explain payload in policy service (cached, TTL 10m) with truncated vectors and reason codes. UI team can surface this in Console's "Why was I throttled" flow.

anne: action items: @sahil - prototype weight publish + local scoring (owner) ; @maria - add sim scenarios using last 30 days of traces; @kevin - design explainability payload shape; @lia - add router cache TTL guidance to runbook. aim for small staging canary by next Friday.

lia: one more thing — preemptive eviction must be cooperative with model-level cache warmup signals. say we evict a request for a large KV-heavy context — we should avoid immediate reroutes that cause cold-start storms. track warmup tokens and penalize eviction_score accordingly.

anne: noted — add warmup_penalty term to score and surface as telemetry. leaving this thread open for follow-ups, please drop links to PRs/sim runs here. :thumbsup:
